text: Electric atmosphere from start to finish — the performance was world-class.
Decent show but the venue's sightlines were poor from the back rows.
Terrible organisation — queues stretched around the block and we missed the first act entirely.
Spectacular light show and the best sound quality I have ever heard live.
Enjoyable event overall, though food stalls ran out of options by mid-afternoon.
Performers were 90 minutes late and the cancellation announcement came via a single tweet.
Wonderful family atmosphere — the kids were captivated and the hosts were warm.
The concept was interesting but execution felt rushed and under-rehearsed.
Great variety of acts and the venue layout meant you were never far from a stage.
Overpriced for what was essentially a community fair dressed up as a premium event.
Unforgettable night — the headline act played three encores and the crowd energy was incredible.
Average experience — neither the worst nor the best event I have attended this year.
Beautifully curated programme with a strong balance of emerging and established artists.
Parking chaos added two hours to our evening and the toilet facilities were disgraceful.
Immersive staging that made you feel part of the story — already buying tickets for next year.
Great selection of local craft vendors; the live folk music added a lovely ambient backdrop.
Sound system kept cutting out mid-set — the technical team seemed unprepared for the crowd size.
The opening ceremony alone was worth the ticket price — truly spectacular pyrotechnics.
Confusing layout and poor signage made it hard to navigate between stages.
One of those rare events that exceeds every expectation — unforgettable performances all round.

Well-organised queuing system with multiple bag-check points; security was thorough but fast.
The headliner cancelled an hour before the show and the replacement was a local support act.
Intimate venue setting meant even the cheap tickets gave a brilliant view of the stage.
Decent event overall though the merchandise stall ran out of programmes by midday.

Long waits at every food and drink stall; the cashless payment system crashed repeatedly.
The comedy line-up was perfectly pitched — mix of emerging acts and established names.
Overcrowded beyond safe limits; I had to leave early as the crowd pressure near the stage felt dangerous.
Smooth entry with QR code scanning; the warm-up act was surprisingly better than expected.
The fireworks finale was extraordinary — timed perfectly to the closing score.
The acoustic quality in the outer sections of the venue was noticeably worse than the floor.
Great charity component to the event — we felt our attendance actually contributed to something positive.
Too many commercial sponsors with their logos dominating every surface — completely killed the atmosphere.
The street food village was as good as the performances; we spent the whole day eating our way around.
Middle-of-the-road experience — worth attending once but not something to travel specifically for.

Half the scheduled activities were moved indoors with no explanation; the outdoor programme was gutted.
The late-night DJ set in the forest clearing was the best surprise discovery of the weekend.
The app kept showing wrong tent locations and staff gave contradictory directions.
Perfectly sized event — big enough to have scale but small enough to feel personal and accessible.
Some strong performances but the programme lacked cohesion — felt more like a grab-bag than a curated festival.
The craft market alongside the main stage was a wonderful addition — bought gifts for everyone back home.
The event started ninety minutes late with no explanation or apology from the organisers.
Every performer delivered something extraordinary — this has become an unmissable annual event for our family.
Ticket prices do not reflect the actual production values — feels like a premium charge for a mid-tier experience.
Accessible entrances were well signed and staff were genuinely helpful to our group member using a wheelchair.
Seating was first-come-first-served despite tickets having numbered seats printed on them — total chaos.

Solid community event with a genuine local flavour — not flashy but heartfelt.
